bomb the city: During the war, enemy planes began to bomb the city at night, and families hid underground.
戰爭期間，敵機開始在夜間轟炸城市，家家戶戶躲到地下。
the movie bombed: Even with famous actors, the movie bombed and lost millions of dollars at the box office.
即使有知名演員，這部電影票房慘敗，損失數百萬美元。
bomb the test: I stayed up playing games instead of studying, so I totally bombed the test this morning.
我熬夜打電動沒讀書，結果今天早上完全考砸了。
bond with the baby: Doctors say that holding and singing to newborns helps parents bond with the baby.
醫生說，抱著新生兒並對他唱歌有助父母與寶寶建立情感。
bond over music: The two shy students bonded over music and soon became best friends in the school band.
那兩位害羞的學生因音樂結緣，很快在校樂隊成了好朋友。
a strong bond: After years of playing on the same team, the players formed a strong bond like brothers.
在同一隊打球多年後，球員們建立了如兄弟般緊密的連結。
the economy is booming: The economy is booming, so many companies are hiring and young people can find jobs easily.
經濟正蓬勃發展，所以許多公司在招人，年輕人很容易找到工作。
business boomed: When bubble tea became popular, business boomed and the small shop opened ten new stores.
珍珠奶茶流行起來後，生意興隆，那家小店新開了十家分店。
a baby boom: After the war ended, there was a baby boom, and many new schools had to be built.
戰爭結束後出現了嬰兒潮，必須興建許多新學校。
thunder boomed: Thunder boomed across the sky, and the frightened dog hid under my bed all night.
雷聲在天空中隆隆作響，受驚的狗整晚躲在我床底下。
boost sales: The shop gave away free cups to boost sales during the slow summer months.
這家店在淡季的夏季月份免費送杯子以提升銷售。
boost confidence: Praise from teachers can boost confidence in students who are afraid of speaking English.
老師的讚美能增強害怕說英語的學生的信心。
boost the economy: The government gave every citizen shopping coupons to boost the economy after the pandemic.
疫情過後，政府發給每位國民消費券以振興經濟。
boost morale: The coach told funny stories in the locker room to boost morale before the final match.
教練在更衣室講笑話，在決賽前鼓舞士氣。
boost one's immune system: Eating fresh fruit and sleeping well can boost your immune system during flu season.
在流感季節吃新鮮水果、睡眠充足能增強你的免疫系統。
boot up the computer: Every morning, the first thing I do at the office is boot up the computer and check my email.
每天早上到辦公室，我做的第一件事就是開機並查看電子郵件。
be booted out: The noisy fans were booted out of the stadium after they threw bottles onto the field.
那些吵鬧的球迷把瓶子丟進場內後被趕出了體育場。
boot someone off the team: The coach had to boot him off the team because he kept missing practice without a reason.
教練不得不把他踢出隊伍，因為他一直無故缺席練習。
bounce back from failure: Successful people know how to bounce back from failure and try again with a new plan.
成功的人懂得從失敗中振作，帶著新計畫再試一次。
the check bounced: The check bounced because there wasn't enough money in his bank account.
因為他的銀行帳戶裡錢不夠，那張支票跳票了。
bounce ideas off someone: Before writing my report, I like to bounce ideas off my classmates to see what they think.
寫報告之前，我喜歡和同學交流想法，看看他們怎麼想。
bounce an email: The system will bounce an email back to you if you type the address incorrectly.
如果你打錯地址，系統會把電子郵件退信給你。
be bound for Taipei: The last train bound for Taipei leaves at eleven, so we must hurry to the station.
開往台北的末班火車十一點開，所以我們得趕快去車站。
be bound to fail: A plan without enough money or support is bound to fail, no matter how good it sounds.
沒有足夠資金或支持的計畫注定失敗，不管聽起來多好。
be bound by rules: All players are bound by rules of fair play and must accept the referee's decisions.
所有球員都受公平競賽規定約束，必須接受裁判的判決。
bound up with: For many Taiwanese people, the Lunar New Year is closely bound up with family and food.
對許多台灣人來說，農曆新年與家人和美食密切相關。
brake hard: A cat suddenly ran into the street, and the bus driver had to brake hard to avoid it.
一隻貓突然衝到街上，公車司機不得不緊急煞車避開牠。
put the brakes on spending: After losing his job, my uncle had to put the brakes on spending and stop eating out.
失業後，我叔叔不得不抑制開支，不再外食。
brake on growth: High house prices act as a brake on growth because young families cannot afford to buy homes.
高房價成為成長的煞車，因為年輕家庭買不起房子。
